a.text: Bumping into an old friend isn't necessarily a good thing for a Sarkaz.
I may not be a Sarkaz, but I know to come prepared.
When you're a kid, you're naive and stupid. A little camaraderie is enough to get you handing over your heartfelt trust.
Even if the place where you built that camaraderie stinks as bad as Kazdel.

Eventually, at some point, you grow up. Maybe it's the first time you kill someone, maybe it's the first time you almost bleed out, or maybe it's the first time you crawled out from under a pile of corpses.

You start learning how to live in the grown-up world. You can be ruthless, you use any means necessary, you can even throw your friends under the bus just to live on, and nobody will hold it against you.
And then, that contrived plot comes around, and you bump into an old friend.
Honestly, after all these years apart, even if you're old friends, do you really have that much to talk about?
It's just... when you were young and stupid, you handed over that trust, you built a 'friendship'.
But when you're at that age, you have the unique opportunity to talk about 'friendship' in Kazdel without being laughed at.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Ulšulah, we're done unloading. They're counting everything in at the warehouse.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Same as before: steel, pure gold, Originium, stuff like that. There hasn't been a personnel transport in weeks. Sounds like most of the forces from the Royal Court in Kazdel are already here.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: That makes things easier on us. Back when the Royal Court guys were floating around, they'd come down here and complain to us, made all sorts of trouble.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Stop.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: That's enough for now.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Oh, sorry.

steps.name: Tired Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Hey, uh, Commander, I've been posted to the waystation for six months now. According to the rotation schedule, it's about time for me to—

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I haven't received any new orders for you.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: But... your performance speaks for itself. I could approve three days of leave for you.

steps.name: Cheering Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Ohh♪ Our Ulšulah♪

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: But don't let it go to your head, make sure to stay grounded.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: All your life in Kazdel, you were a cobbler. Your greatest accomplishment is nailing soles together. What are you in the running for, unless you're prepared to blow yourself up?

steps.name: Cheering Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: Ulšulah♪ You're no fun♪

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Get outta here, kid.

a.text: I watch Ulšulah's profile, the corners of her mouth curling up.
Thinking back... back to then.
She carries herself the same way, at least.
The young Sarkaz cobbler approaches Hoederer and slyly hands him a flask.

steps.name: Slyly Smiling Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: (Whispering) Hey, brother, hold onto this for me. Ulšulah can't go a day without the stuff.

steps.name: Slyly Smiling Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: (Whispering) You're really something, man, walking around with this piece at your side, and still—

a.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Watch your mouth, cobbler.

steps.name: Fleeing Sarkaz Worker
steps.text: What's sweeter than honey♪ What's toxic as nightshade♪

a.text: Looks like he hasn't even had his coming-of-age yet. Those years with Her Highness Theresa did a lot to see these kids grow up nice and sheltered.
And now, he's in a war out here by Londinium. Hah, brother and sister joined hands to create the worst joke in history.
If only it wasn't a joke.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: If you open that notebook, I'm setting it on fire.

a.text: Hoederer quietly tucks away his notebook.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You two haven't changed. That's nice.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: It's been years.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Since that operation.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Me, Hoederer and W... the old W, got ourselves into trouble, killed some people we shouldn't have killed.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: It's not just the Scar Market, showing your faces in Kazdel would be trouble for you.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I see your names there a lot... on the bounty lists. You're famous.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: I've never been a cheap date.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Sure enough. Ines's investment paid off well.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: We were all so young.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Getting old now?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I'm a Sarkaz, you're a sheep. In theory, I'm gonna live longer than you, Ines.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: We're all Infected, so this isn't about racial lifespans.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Good point. I'll drink to you and wish myself good health.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: ——ahhh.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I remember you used to say that if a Sarkaz wants to live long, she needs to keep a clear head, before somebody else trades it for coin.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Whoever wants it can take it. Victorian, Sarkaz, doesn't matter to me.

a.text: She leans in close, sizing me up, then glances at Hoederer.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You've got wrinkles, Ines.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: I died three times and only got a few wrinkles to show for it. I should thank the myriad souls.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You don't thank them, you're a sheep.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: As for Hoederer, you're missing an eye.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Wanna see the socket? It's all thanks to the fine Caprinae woman right here.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Lose an eye, or lose your head. You had a choice.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I guess Ines broke her heart when she made the move.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: ...Drop it.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We're old friends getting together again, can't we get back to a nice atmosphere of sentimental nostalgia?

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Talk about days gone by, muse on the passage of time...

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We could talk about how you became the youngest major in the Military Commission, the driver of this skeletal Feranmut, Commander Ulšulah.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Yes... we should talk about that. Otherwise, we being who we are, we shouldn't be so warm and friendly.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: And we could also talk about you, these two Sarkaz...

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: One Sarkaz traitor, and one sheep. Why are you popping up at a secret Military Commission site?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I know you were detained by General Manfred, Hoederer.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: And you and Ines, who disrupted our operations, together with an obnoxious little girl planting bombs all around, stole into my territory, in broad daylight.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: As an officer of the Military Commission, I can't very well let that go.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's two against one here, Ulšulah.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Is it? Remind me, where are we again?

a.text: Huh, since when?
The girl wasn't like this before.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You're welcome to try, Ines.

a.text: She's wearing a smile, but she's dead serious.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: The most important thing I've learned over the years is to be true to my decisions.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: And Theresis is your decision?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: No, the Military Commission is.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You decided to go with Babel—Or what is it called now? Rhodes Island? And I decided to stand with the Commission.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: We decided our paths a long time ago.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ulšulah, we can still—

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I know what you want, Hoederer, you haven't changed a bit.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: But we're not those kids who strutted around cheery for a whole day on the back of a single bounty anymore.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: We don't get to relax after our missions these days, no idle afternoons on the streets of Kazdel.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: We are Sarkaz... or at least we're citizens of Kazdel. It's our responsibility to make those streets and alleys a better place.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Kazdel is the main issue here, Ulšulah!

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Then you've gotta admit, the Military Commission is the best choice we've got! Even Her Highness Theresa wouldn't disagree!

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: It was the two royals who made Kazdel into a nomadic city, the both of them who made it possible for us to even talk about the future of the Sarkaz here!

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: It was the same two royals who promoted me, giving a poor girl from the slums a chance to stand in the sight of the Royal Court, among those pure and ancient bloodlines.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Once trapped by naivety and compromise, the Sarkaz lose our chance at a true homeland.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: There's no room for me to hesitate here.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: The Military Commission, it's... it's the foundation for Kazdel to become a nation.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Will there even be a Kazdel once this war is over?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: All I know is I'm no traitor.

a.text: Sure, we were prepared to bump into this old friend from the beginning.
Hoederer tacitly crosses from my side to confront this stupid girl, the Major of the Military Commission.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Ten minutes, that's my limit.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: Get as much intel on that thing as you can.

a.text: I bypass several Sarkaz blocking my way, shadows entwining their ankles.
I leap up, climbing the nerve clusters of this terrifying creature, the slippery feeling making me slightly sick.
Is this a Feranmut? I've never seen one before.
Show me the secrets hiding in your mind.
This isn't a good section to walk on.
My luck has been pretty bad lately, always ending up in the body of some kind of monster. Last time it was the revenant, this time it's whatever this is.
Ugh, I hope I don't have to jump off it this time.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: These 'nails' piercing its spine must be some kind of witchcraft device.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Are those nerve clusters trembling? Does this thing still have a will of its own?

steps.name: Spine Guardian
steps.text: She's here!

a.text: Ugh, how are they so quick? They climb up the skeleton in hot pursuit.
The sinews between the bones become something like a ladder for them, with the splinters of fallen bone serving as their weapons.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hm, they know war. Ulšulah's trained a real elite unit.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: But they could stand to work in some variety.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: All they've got on me is numbers—

a.text: A foreboding instinct pops into my head and I instinctively dodge to the side.
A huge cluster of nerves comes crashing down, and the bone fragments I have been standing on shatter and crumble.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's so hard on itself.

a.text: Hmph, looks like every bone fragment, every bundle of sinew here could be a deadly weapon. That's a pain.
The nerve cluster wraps around again. I sink my dagger into it so hard that it recoils violently, carrying me high into the air.
Alright, so it has the most basic of reflexes.
Good enough. There's a cabin up ahead.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Right there!

a.text: With all my might, I grab the dangling bundle of nerves and leap away.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Dust everywhere... from wind-weathered bone.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: This should be the center.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hm, no clear interface. Is it driven purely by witchcraft?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: A willing slave? Or a marionette controlled by strings?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hmmm...

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You dodged my Arts, Ines. That should've gone right through your heart.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You still haven't fixed that old habit of yours, your casting always deviates a little to the left.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Lucky I've been on the bad end of that enough times.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You in a hurry? Did Hoederer make a fool out of you?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: It's fragile, isn't it? Not as honest as it seems.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You're welcome to guess.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: If we get the chance, I'd really like to hear about those three deaths you mentioned. Must be a thrilling story.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: You wanna try once?

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: No, I'd rather us live.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: If you can make it through the chaos and live on, that is.

a.text: A tremendous force flips me over, the nerve bundle sweeps away, trying to tug me with it. The Feranmut is gradually swinging its body.
They've built a lot of cabins here.
And the thing tends to drift in the space.
What if the Feranmut wanders when I'm not in one of the cabins?
I really don't want to find out.
I'm not Hoederer, I'm not into becoming history.
Shadows, like blades, sweep through the hall of bone.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Save what's left of your dignity, Ines, there's no point.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Your shadows can't protect you from the might of a Feranmut.

a.text: Weathered bone dust takes flight again, filling my vision.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Thanks for the reminder.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hoederer—!

a.text: Oftentimes, even I have to admit that Hoederer makes a pretty good partner.
I'm actually glad we didn't betray each other. It's hard to find a Sarkaz like him.
The past was tough, and the future's gonna be tough too.
The dim firelight rises with the dust, twisting.
His figure emerges from the embers, sparks in the wind singe his cloak and my hair.
And sometimes... only sometimes... I'm willing to tolerate his obnoxious Arts.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: We're well past the age when we can talk about friendship.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: But I'd rather live in a future Kazdel that keeps the 'silly' naivety we always laughed at.

a.text: The turbulence is intensifying.
I grab his hand.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: Sigh...

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: I forgot to tell you, Hoederer. General Manfred gave me your book.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: It's pretty good, I have to admit.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: You gathered up the bits and pieces, arranging them in chronological order, thinking you found the thread.

steps.name: Ulšulah
steps.text: But you've been running all this time. Do you plan to do this forever?

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Drop it, Ulšulah, time to say goodbye.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Hoederer, you're jumping with me this time.

steps.name: Ines
steps.text: Don't get swept away by the turbulence of history. Never forget the present... the life that you're living.

steps.name: Hoederer
steps.text: You're the boss.

a.text: Boiling shadows point the way for us, scorched dust carrying us along.
The illusions shift before our eyes.
When I'm falling fast enough, I suddenly realize that history really does look pretty fragile and hypocritical.
I see a vast, and familiar battlefield. One of the war zones from Kazdel, where the flames are still burning.
I recall the past. Hoederer always wanted to steer clear of the war that tore apart his people. I force myself to turn my head, while he's single-mindedly focused on finding a suitable landing zone.
Run away from the war? Heh.
We weren't at Babel when Her Highness came under attack. We could have left Kazdel straight away. Why did we go back for W?
Why join Reunion? Why lay low in Londinium all this time?
What is Hoederer fighting for anyway?
What am I... fighting for?
We break through the earth, the illusions vanish, and we see what was always there.
He grabs my arm, telling me to be ready.
Arts envelop us and my vision clears. Shadows rise from the ground.
Maybe we stopped running a long time ago.
